name: de Young Museum
address: 50 Hagiwara Tea Garden Dr, San Francisco, CA 94118
description: Anchor of the city's fine-arts collection; the Hamon Tower observation level is one of the calmest views in the city.
why: American painting, photography, and a Herzog & de Meuron building that's worth the visit on its own.

name: Legion of Honor
description: Beaux-Arts pavilion above the Pacific with European masters and one of the world's great Rodin collections.
why: The setting, the building, and the Rodin galleries — rare in any American museum.

name: Holocaust Memorial
description: George Segal's white-painted bronze installation (1984) in a grove just outside the Legion of Honor.
why: A quiet, piercing piece set on a hill above the bay — free, outdoors, and easily missed.

name: SFMOMA
description: Seven floors of modern and contemporary art with one of the strongest photography wings on the West Coast.
why: The Snøhetta expansion opened a building you want to wander, beyond what's on the walls.

name: Museum of the African Diaspora
description: Three floors of contemporary art of the African diaspora inside the St. Regis tower.
why: Smaller and more focused than SFMOMA — easily absorbed in an hour.

name: Berggruen Gallery
description: Long-established SF gallery for modern and contemporary painting, around the corner from SFMOMA.
why: Understated, well-lit, and a quiet final stop after a museum afternoon.

name: Asian Art Museum
description: One of the largest Asian art collections in the West, in a Beaux-Arts library reworked by Gae Aulenti.
why: Calm galleries at an unhurried scale, and rotating shows worth checking the calendar for.

name: Davies Symphony Hall
address: 201 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: Home of the San Francisco Symphony — a purpose-built 1980 hall on Van Ness.
why: Check the season for Mahler or Tchaikovsky with a guest conductor of the week.

name: War Memorial Opera House
address: 301 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: Home of San Francisco Opera and San Francisco Ballet, in a 1932 Beaux-Arts hall.
why: Dress up. Catch The Barber of Seville or whatever SF Ballet is mounting that month.

name: SFJAZZ Center
description: Purpose-built jazz hall with a year-round calendar across two stages.
why: Smaller, more intimate room than the symphony — and the booking is consistently great.

name: Minnesota Street Project
description: Purpose-built complex housing eleven contemporary galleries under one roof.
why: An efficient survey of what San Francisco's commercial art scene is doing.

name: Museum of Craft and Design
description: Small museum of contemporary craft, design, and material art — one floor, a few rooms.
why: The scale is right for an after-coffee visit; one or two thoughtful shows at a time.

name: Grace Cathedral
description: Episcopal cathedral with a Ghiberti Gates of Paradise, a Keith Haring altarpiece, and two labyrinths.
why: A cool, quiet interior on top of Nob Hill — built for slow walking and slow looking.

name: Jessica Silverman
description: Contemporary gallery with a strong roster of mid-career artists.
why: Crisply curated — a short, satisfying visit.

name: Fraenkel Gallery
description: Canonical photography gallery — Arbus, Friedlander, Sugimoto, Fuss — in a building of a dozen galleries.
why: If photography is of interest, Fraenkel is the West Coast destination.

name: Fort Mason Center for Arts & Culture
description: Former military complex turned arts campus on the bay; home to FOR-SITE and rotating exhibitions.
why: Bay views, a contemplative pace, and shows you won't see elsewhere.

name: Ferry Building
description: The restored 1898 ferry terminal — a public marketplace by day, civic landmark by all hours.
why: Coffee, oysters, ceramics, books — the polished, walkable interior is the whole pleasure.

name: Sausalito (the crossing)
description: A 25-minute Golden Gate Ferry crossing with full views of the bay and bridge — the ride is the experience.
why: Brunch at the Ferry Building, ferry over, walk Bridgeway, return on a later sailing.

name: Sausalito Center for the Arts
description: Community arts center on Bridgeway with rotating juried exhibitions in painting, sculpture, and photography.
why: Two blocks from the ferry landing — a quick, civilized stop on the Sausalito leg.

name: Filoli
description: 1917 Georgian-revival house and sixteen acres of Italianate gardens — sunken garden, knot garden, long pool.
why: The most rewarding garden visit within reach of the city; bonsai exhibition through May.

name: Saison
description: Open-hearth, ingredient-driven Californian tasting menu in a brick-walled former power station.
why: For the ritual of cooking over live flame, taken to its absolute peak.

name: Lazy Bear
description: Modern American tasting menu served around long communal tables — half dinner party, half theater.
why: Going alone? You'll leave with new friends. Going with friends? You'll leave with new ones too.

name: Nari
description: Pim Techamuanvivit's California-seasoned Thai — laab with artichokes, massaman curry with cherries.
why: Bold, fearless cooking in a sexy, plant-filled room — date-night without being precious.

name: Acquerello
description: Suzette Gresham's white-tablecloth Italian — the famed black-truffle ridged pasta is its calling card.
why: For the most polished, hushed Italian fine-dining experience in the city.

name: Kin Khao
address: 55 Cyril Magnin St, San Francisco, CA 94102
description: Pim Techamuanvivit's first restaurant — fiery, herb-laden Thai using small Northern California producers.
why: Crispy duck noodle soup, tamarind-glazed wings, and curries you'll think about for weeks.

name: State Bird Provisions
description: Servers wheel rotating carts of small plates referencing Asia, Mexico, Europe — pick what looks good.
why: An anti-tasting-menu — the most fun way to eat ambitious food in San Francisco.

name: Mijoté
description: Tiny bistro from a Japanese chef trained in Paris — four-course set menu, wild natural-wine list.
why: Open Mondays, generously portioned, and unlike anything else in San Francisco.

name: Zuni Café
description: Roast chicken for two with bread salad, oysters at the copper bar — the city's most enduring icon.
why: Order the chicken when you sit down — it takes an hour, and it's worth every minute.

name: Rich Table
description: Sardine chips, porcini doughnuts, douglas-fir levain — Sarah and Evan Rich's craveable, signature menu.
why: Service that knows what it's doing, food that makes you smile, ten years of consistency.

name: The Progress
description: Family-style menu of shareable plates from State Bird's siblings — pick four, the kitchen sends everything.
why: The choose-your-own-adventure format makes it perfect for groups of six.

name: Outerlands
description: Ocean Beach hideout serving sourdough, grilled-cheese-and-soup, and seasonal Cal cuisine.
why: After a long beach walk, there is no better place to land for brunch or dinner.

name: Octavia
description: Melissa Perello's Pac Heights anchor — the city's best Cal cuisine done quietly and exactly right.
why: Approachable refinement: deviled eggs, coastal halibut, cappelletti — every plate considered.

name: Spruce
description: Polished Sacramento Street dining room with one of the city's most serious cellars and a famed burger.
why: Old-world service, banquettes built for special occasions, a cellar built for collectors.

name: Cotogna
description: Quince's casual sister: handmade pasta, the famed egg-yolk raviolo, focaccia di recco.
why: More accessible than Quince, less edgy than Verjus — beloved by everyone.

name: Flour + Water
description: Eighty-three pasta shapes a year — McNaughton and Pollnow's pasta-and-Neapolitan-pizza flagship.
why: Splurge on the pasta tasting menu; it's one of the city's defining special-occasion meals.

name: Penny Roma
description: Roman-leaning trattoria from the Flour + Water team — cacio e pepe, suppli, fritto misto.
why: When you want all the F+W technique with the swagger of a Trastevere dinner.

name: Delfina
description: Twenty-six years of perfect spaghetti, grilled calamari over white beans, and marinated anchovies.
why: The dictionary definition of al dente — the version of Italian everyone else copies.

name: Che Fico
description: Fragrant rotisserie meats and bright Italian-Jewish cooking under playful patterned wallpaper.
why: Crowd-pleasing Italian that still surprises — the carciofi alla giudia is a must.

name: SPQR
description: Pasta-driven menu rotating through Italy's regions, by chef Matthew Accarrino — refined, deeply technical.
why: If pasta is your love language, SPQR speaks it more fluently than almost anyone.

name: A16
description: Naples-inspired pizza, ricotta gnudi, and burrata with a wine list deep on Campanian whites.
why: Twenty years in and still the best Southern Italian in town.

name: Original Joe's
description: Red leather booths, white-jacketed waiters, calf's liver and Joe's special — old-school Italian-American.
why: Time-capsule SF. Order a martini, a cassata for dessert, and pretend it's 1947.

name: Piccino
description: Sunny corner trattoria in a yellow Victorian — wood-fired pizza, antipasti, and vegetable-forward pasta.
why: Wander Dogpatch's galleries, then land here for an unhurried lunch on the patio.

name: Poesia
description: Warm Castro osteria serving authentic Calabrian-leaning regional Italian since 2008.
why: A taste of southern Italy you won't find easily elsewhere in the city.

name: Rose's Cafe
description: All-day Cal-Italian café on Union — house-made pastas, breakfast pizzas, sidewalk seating.
why: The best brunch in Cow Hollow, with a long, sun-soaked lunch built right in.

name: Tony's Pizza Napoletana
description: Thirteen ovens, every regional pizza style done correctly, plus pasta and salads.
why: The Margherita STG is one of only a few certified-Neapolitan pies in the country.

name: Del Popolo
description: Glass-walled wood oven, blistered Neapolitan pies, market-driven seasonal toppings.
why: Some of the best Neapolitan pizza in the country, in a room you'll want to linger in.

name: Pizzeria Delfina
description: Thin, charred pies with serious toppings — broccoli rabe, fennel sausage, salt cod.
why: The salumi pie with a glass of red is the easiest perfect dinner in town.

name: Capo's
description: Sister to Tony's — deep-dish, tavern-style, and stuffed Chicago pies in a clubby red room.
why: When you specifically need a deep-dish in a city of thin crusts.

name: Flour + Water Pizzeria
description: Casual Valencia pizza spinoff: Neapolitan and Detroit pies plus salads and pastas.
why: Walk-in friendly, slice-shop fast, with the F+W team's pasta DNA in the dough.

name: Galinette
description: Provençal-leaning seafood from the Petit Marlowe team — bouillabaisse, plateaux, sea urchin pasta.
why: The polished French seafood spot San Francisco was missing.

name: Le Marais Bakery & Bistro
description: Genuine French boulangerie + sidewalk bistro — kouign-amann, croque-monsieur, steak-frites.
why: Brunch on the patio with a basket of pastries — the closest thing to a Paris café in SF.

name: Frances
description: Melissa Perello's Castro original — a daily-changing menu of California ingredients in a warm room.
why: Tiny dining room, white wines on tap by the ounce, cooking that has aged beautifully.

name: Chez Maman
description: Cozy bistro for moules-frites, croque-monsieurs, and crepes — counter seating around an open kitchen.
why: Casual, candle-lit, and the kind of dinner that feels effortless on a weeknight.

name: Robin
description: No-menu omakase in a stylish wood-paneled room — vinyl on the turntable, sake list to match.
why: Fish flown in daily, paired with a pulse — the loosest, most fun omakase in town.

name: Marufuku Ramen
description: Creamy 20-hour Hakata-style tonkotsu broth and thin straight noodles — the bowl people line up for.
why: The richest, most satisfying ramen in the city — worth the inevitable wait.

name: Iza Ramen
description: Tightly run noodle bar — tonkotsu, miso, shoyu, plus killer izakaya snacks and shochu cocktails.
why: When you want ramen plus a karaage and a highball, all in 45 minutes.

name: HK Lounge Bistro
description: Annie Ho's Hong Kong Lounge II reborn in SoMa — pristine har gow, chive dumplings, salted-egg buns.
why: The best dim sum in the city, served with the warmth and care of a neighborhood restaurant.

name: R&G Lounge
description: Salt-and-pepper crab is the dish that built the reputation — order it, plus the clay pot rice.
why: A Chinatown institution that gets it right night after night.

name: China Live
description: George Chen's three-floor showcase — open kitchens for Peking duck, dim sum, hot pot, dumplings.
why: An interactive Chinese food experience that's part restaurant, part edible museum.

name: Mama Ji's
description: Tiny Castro spot for fiery mapo tofu, dan dan noodles, and rare home-style Sichuan dim sum.
why: Spicy without being macho — actual Sichuan flavors at neighborhood prices.

name: Dumpling Time
description: Soup dumplings, pork buns, gyoza, and a giant XLB you eat with a straw — Asian dumplings, all of them.
why: Lively, walk-in friendly, and the dumplings are genuinely excellent.

name: La Taqueria
description: Charred carne asada, no rice — the quietly perfect Mission burrito, ordered dorado (seared).
why: Decades-long debate winner. Order the burrito with everything, dorado, with avocado.

name: El Farolito
description: Massive, cheap, made-to-order burritos open until 2:30 a.m. — al pastor and shrimp are the moves.
why: The post-bar burrito, but also a perfectly fine lunch.

name: Nopalito
description: Bay Area-organic regional Mexican from the Nopa team — masa pressed in-house, mole, carnitas.
why: Refined Mexican that doesn't try to be fancy, just deeply done well.

name: Coqueta
address: Pier 5, The Embarcadero, San Francisco, CA 94111
description: Waterfront pintxos and paella, with bay views and a serious sherry list.
why: Sit on the patio at dusk with a glass of cava and a plate of jamón — pure SF.

name: Turtle Tower
description: Northern (Hanoi) pho with wide rice noodles and clear, ginger-forward chicken broth.
why: If your idea of pho is the cilantro-bean-sprout version, this will gently rewrite it.

name: Lers Ros
description: Pages-long menu of regional Thai, including the harder-to-find dishes — boar, frog, herb-heavy salads.
why: Open until 1 a.m. and willing to bring the heat when you ask — the city's most reliable Thai.

name: Farmhouse Kitchen Thai
description: Bright, modern Thai with Instagram-friendly cocktails and standout massaman curry and khao soi.
why: Group dinner heaven — flavorful, photogenic, and never overrun.

name: Hawker Fare
description: James Syhabout's Lao-Isan rice plates — papaya salad, larb, sticky rice, jeow dipping sauces.
why: An education in Lao food, served casually and without fuss.

name: Burma Superstar
description: The tea-leaf salad that started a Bay Area Burmese craze — plus samusa soup and rainbow salad.
why: If you've never had Burmese food, start here. If you have, you already know.

name: Burma Love
description: Sister to Burma Superstar, brighter dining room — same tea leaf salad, same rich curries.
why: All the Burma Superstar greatest hits with a more polished setting and easier reservations.

name: Copra
description: Srijith Gopinathan's coastal South Indian — extravagant chutney platters, banana-leaf cod, rasam puri.
why: The most exhilarating Indian restaurant in the country right now, in a stunning room.

name: Tiya
description: Modern New Indian by chefs Sujan and Pujan Sarkar — Indian flavors with California's seasonal bounty.
why: Bold, creative, beautifully plated Indian — try the tasting menu for the full picture.

name: Amber India
address: 25 Yerba Buena Ln, San Francisco, CA 94103
description: Spacious modern Indian with sandstone latticework — butter chicken, biryanis, naan from the tandoor.
why: The polished Indian destination near downtown — great for a pre-show meal.

name: Daeho Kalbijjim & Beef Soup
description: The iconic short-rib galbijjim — braised, cheese-blanketed, served at long communal tables.
why: Loud, fun, fortifying — the city's go-to Korean comfort meal in a group of 4+.

name: Aziza
description: Mourad Lahlou's quietly remarkable Moroccan — basteeya, lamb tagine, the famous Moroccan pancakes.
why: Twenty years on Geary, still one of the most singular dining rooms in the city.

name: Kokkari Estiatorio
description: Whole roasted lamb, charcoal-grilled fish, hand-stretched filo — taverna grandeur in Jackson Square.
why: The spit-roast lamb is one of the great main courses in San Francisco.

name: Dalida
description: Turkish, Greek, and Lebanese flavors in a brick-walled landmark — labneh, kebabs, tahdig with trout roe.
why: One of the most beautiful new dining rooms in SF, pointed at the Parade Lawn.

name: Milos Meze
description: Family-run Marina Greek — oregano lamb chops, bubbling saganaki, the city's best souvlaki.
why: Modest room, no pretension, food worth driving across town for.

name: Lokma
description: Bright Turkish-influenced all-day spot — sucuk-and-eggs, simit, mezze, lamb kofte.
why: Brunch or dinner, the menu always over-delivers for the price.

name: Señor Sisig
description: Sisig burritos, tacos, and rice bowls — the truck-turned-empire that everyone in SF has tried.
why: Comfort food crossover that genuinely works — get the tofu sisig if you don't eat pork.

name: Limón
address: 1001 S Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94110
description: Ceviches, lomo saltado, anticuchos — twenty years of bright, briny Peruvian classics.
why: A rotisserie chicken and a pisco sour is the dinner deal of the Mission.

name: Hog Island Oyster Co.
description: Briny Tomales Bay oysters at the Ferry Building, plus chowder and the famed grilled cheese.
why: Sit at the bar facing the water with a dozen Sweetwaters — pure California.

name: Woodhouse Fish Co.
description: New England-style fish shack — lobster rolls, oysters, fried clams, ice-cold beer.
why: When you want a lobster roll on a Tuesday and don't want to fly to Maine.

name: House of Prime Rib
address: 1906 Van Ness Ave, San Francisco, CA 94109
description: Carved-tableside prime rib from gleaming silver carts — the only main course on the menu.
why: The hardest reservation in San Francisco and worth every minute of the wait.

name: Schroeder's
description: Wiener schnitzel, sauerbraten, liter steins — SF's oldest German beer hall, refreshed.
why: Lederhosen-optional. The pretzel and a stein at happy hour is exactly what FiDi was missing.

name: Tartine Bakery
description: Country bread, morning buns, frangipane croissants — the bakery that taught a generation about bread.
why: Stand in line for the morning bun. Stand in line again for the country bread at 4:30 p.m.

name: Tartine Manufactory
description: Bigger Tartine sibling — full menu of sandwiches, bowls, and pastries plus an in-house ice cream bar.
why: When you want Tartine the bakery and Tartine the restaurant in one stop.

name: Arsicault Bakery
description: Outer Richmond's small French bakery turning out arguably the country's best croissants.
why: Get there before 11 a.m. or risk being out of luck.

name: b. patisserie
description: Belinda Leong's pastry temple — kouign-amann, canelés, and sablé tarts that disappear by noon.
why: The kouign-amann is the city's standard. Pair with an espresso, sit in the window.

name: Neighbor Bakehouse
description: Laminated dough at every angle — everything croissants, kouign-amann, focaccia, sourdough.
why: If laminated pastry is its own art form, Neighbor is the museum.

name: Jane the Bakery
description: Sourdough miches, scones, breakfast pizzas, plus all-day café fare and coffee.
why: Bread you'd be proud to bring to a dinner party — and a perfect breakfast counter.

name: Boulettes Larder
description: Counter-style breakfast and lunch beside the Ferry Building's open kitchen — soulful Cal food.
why: Watch them cook your eggs at the marble counter; bay window seating is the bonus.

name: Dandelion Chocolate
description: Bean-to-bar chocolate factory — single-origin bars, hot chocolate, brownies, the chocolate panini.
why: The Mission Hot Chocolate (75% Madagascar) is one of the best things you'll drink all year.

name: Saint Frank Coffee
description: Bright, minimalist Russian Hill flagship — direct-trade beans, perfect espresso, Friends-team pastries.
why: The cleanest, most precise espresso program in San Francisco.

name: Sightglass Coffee
description: Industrial SoMa flagship with a mezzanine — long bar, deep roast program, cult cold brew.
why: A weekend-morning espresso destination that still feels like a working roaster.

name: Ritual Coffee
description: The Valencia Street original — bright, fruity coffees and a daily-changing single-origin lineup.
why: If you only go to one third-wave shop in SF, make it Ritual.

name: Juniper
description: Saint Frank's bakery sister — viennoiserie, matcha lattes, and the croissant that won SF's best.
why: The most beautiful breakfast pastries in the city, if you can find seats.

name: Plow
description: Lemon-ricotta pancakes, the legendary Plow potatoes, and Hong-Kong-style toast.
why: Worth the wait — go early on a Saturday or accept your fate.

name: Sweet Maple
description: Pacific Heights brunch with the famed Millionaire's Bacon — thick-cut, brown-sugared, peppered.
why: Pancakes, eggs Benedict, and a side of bacon you'll talk about all day.

name: Mama's on Washington Square
description: French toast sampler, Monte Cristo, Dungeness benedict — North Beach brunch worth the line.
why: Show up at 8:30 a.m. or accept a 90-minute wait. It's worth it either way.

name: Zazie
description: Cole Valley French bistro best known for inventive eggs Benedict and the back garden.
why: Brunch in the back garden on a sunny day is one of the city's quiet pleasures.

name: The Mill
description: Josey Baker bread, toasted thick, schmeared with cinnamon-sugar butter or almond butter and honey.
why: The platonic ideal of toast. Yes, just toast. Yes, you should go.

name: Causwells
description: Marina bistro hiding one of SF's best burgers — the Americana, with American cheese and house pickles.
why: Sit at the bar for the burger and a martini, then maybe stay for the rest of the menu.

name: Wise Sons Jewish Deli
description: House-cured pastrami, latkes, matzo ball soup, and a daily black-and-white cookie.
why: A real Jewish deli, in a city that needed one — stay for the chocolate babka.

name: Gott's Roadside
description: Counter-service burgers, ahi tuna burgers, sweet-potato fries, and shakes by the bay.
why: Lunch outside facing the Bay Bridge — a classic SF afternoon.

name: Shizen
description: Vegan sushi that converts skeptics — eggplant nigiri, body-and-soul roll, miso ramen.
why: The clearest argument that sushi can be untethered from fish — and still delicious.

name: Greens Restaurant
address: 2 Marina Blvd Building A, San Francisco, CA 94123
description: The vegetarian dining room that started a national conversation, with a wall of bay windows.
why: Bay views, polished service, and vegetable cooking that even committed carnivores admire.

name: Wildseed
description: Plant-based California cooking that's friendly to all — bowls, tacos, burgers, brunch.
why: The kind of vegan food that doesn't feel like vegan food.

name: Trick Dog
description: Mission warehouse cocktail palace with a menu that reinvents itself twice a year — every concept clever.
why: On every short list of best bars in the country, year after year.

name: ABV
description: A bartender's bar — riff classics, easy-drinking originals, and a kitchen that punches above its weight.
why: The sit-at-the-bar place every SF bartender goes on their night off.

name: True Laurel
description: Lazy Bear's mid-century-modern cocktail spinoff — fermented honey, roasted quince, perfect snacks.
why: Cocktails as ambitious as the food at the Michelin-starred sister.

name: Pagan Idol
description: Wooden-ship interior, erupting volcano in the back room — Tiki Bob's space, taken to its peak.
why: An immersive, escapist tiki experience — perfect for a first date or a last drink.

name: Comstock Saloon
description: Restored Barbary Coast saloon — perfectly mixed classics and a kitchen that goes deep on craft.
why: The most evocative drinking room in the city, with cocktails to match.

name: The Snug
description: Pacific Heights cocktail bar with deep amaro shelves and food that's actually worth ordering.
why: The neighborhood bar you wish was your neighborhood bar.

name: Smuggler's Cove
description: Three-story rum temple — 700+ rums, unflashy expertise, drinks served from a literal pirate ship.
why: If you've ever wondered what tiki does taken seriously, Smuggler's is the answer.

name: 15 Romolo
description: Tucked down an alley off Broadway — punch bowls, snug booths, food that's better than it needs to be.
why: When you want to feel like you've found something secret in the middle of the city.

name: Bourbon & Branch
description: Reservation-only speakeasy with a buzzer at the door — classic cocktails done with reverence.
why: When you want the speakeasy bit done with sincerity instead of theme.

name: Balboa Cafe
description: Cow Hollow saloon institution — the famed Balboa burger on a baguette, espressotinis, regulars at the bar.
why: The kind of bar where you'll know everybody's name by the time you leave.
